chapter: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
title: Touring downriver with Rene Parker
summary: With singer Rene Parker he played Creole numbers and old jazz in Plaquemines Parish towns.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I see. And what about Rene Parker? Did you ever know him?

Oh yeah, I worked with him. I'm going to tell you who I worked with Rene Parker. I used to go down in Platinum, he talks Creole, French. Yeah, I see. Sing French. You know him singing, he was a boy and all that. I used to, you see he had a big banjo player named George. Mm-hmm. And that banjo player died. He started taking me and Walter. Walter Nelson. Mm-hmm.

He used to take us down to Platinum Palace. Mm-hmm. He from down there. I see. He's from down there. He used to take us to Empire, Louisiana, Trank, Louisiana, all down there, and that section. Yeah, I know him. He still alive? Right.
Rainey Parker died in his 70s. Mm-hmm. Died old man. That ain't been, that's been about 12 or 15 years ago.
He sang on Creole numbers. A few, a few numbers he sang, you know. Yeah. But he had Walter, that's what Walter mostly did. He was singing because Walter was no, no exploit player, you know.

Mm-hmm. Well what did René Parker sing? He said Creole, what did I sing Creole? Yeah, he sang. He sang Elabar and things like that, yeah. And what about the people down there in Blackmon? And what number did they like?
Well we played numbers like High Society, Millenburg Joy, no numbers like that.

Yeah. All of what they call now is Dixieland but it's old jazz. Yeah. Like in those days it was old jazz. You see when we used to go down there with René Parker, before you get to your destination you stop on every store gallery.
